general_information.Description: This course will explore existing modern typographical ideas and techniques and attempt to expand on students’ typographical range. Students will investigate the communication of content and the emotional qualities of text. Students will further develop their visual and conceptual fluency and create integrated communication design solutions. Emphasis will be placed on using typography, aesthetics, and composition to construct meaningful imagery and effectively solve communication problems. This course uses the art of typography, aesthetic element,..., to build up ideas and apply them in designing products for graphic design such as: publication, branding systems.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend more than 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfil tasks given by intructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (www.cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment. - Computer with some version of photograph editing software such as Photoshop, Microsoft Word for written assignments, and POWERPOINT for presentations - Have color papers, Color Pencils, scissors... - Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher 1 day after the course.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand typographic and layout conventions used in the work of others
Know terminology used within typographic and layout design
Know grids systems, structural systems, alignments for typographic layout
Apply the principles of hierarchy and dominance to typographic elements.
Create works implementing typographic best practices
Appreciate typography’s role in design and understand its potential for effective communication
Organize words and images in design layouts using typographic structural systems, alignments and grids.
Develop an understanding of the language of typography, which includes critical theory, critique, history, technology, and craftsmanship
Be able to evaluate own typographic and layout design outcomes.

schedule.Student's Tasks: INDIVIDUAL WORK - Starting with the simplest books: novels, memoirs, essays, and narrative nonfiction. - Book construction: Each part of the book has its role to play and its assigned place in the whole. - Cover design basics - Fonts for text: There’s no bigger decision a designer makes than selecting the fonts that will be used for the book’s text. - Fonts for display: Knowing how to choose and combine typefaces is critical for the designer. - Architecture of the book page: Building pages and spreads is at the heart of book design. - Non-text book elements: Every book incorporates elements that are outside the text itself, like notes, bibliographies, part- and chapter-opening pages, captions, sidebars, pull-quotes, and others. Each has to blend well with the rest of the book, and stand out when necessary. - Max 32 paper
- Complete and print Book - Students are responsible for printing the products and paying the printing cost.
